newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slide on political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slide on political uncertainty.

text.p: Slovenian shares lost one percent on Wednesday as uncertainty over what form the new government would take following the November 10 general election continued to keep a lid on active buying.
"Due to the unclear political situation, shares will track sideways in dull trade at least for another month," one said.
Brokers said real market turnover was particularly limp when one stripped away a single massive trade worth 211.5 million tolars in drug company Lek.
Turnover for the whole market reached 269.9 million tolars, up from 95.1 million on Tuesday.

At the election, the centre-left Liberal Democrats of current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek emerged as the strongest single party with 25 out of 90 seats. But the loose alliance of rightist "Spring" parties is trying to form the new government.
The alliance -- comprising the conservative People's Party, the Social Democrats and Christian Democrats -- won a total 45 seats, missing an absolute majority by just one seat.
"If the rightist parties manage to form a new government that would prolong uncertainty on the market due to their cautious stand towards the EU so far," another trader said.
The 10-share SBI index fell 11.06 points to 1,141.6.
Six shares fell, 11 rose, two were unchanged and six were untraded.
Drug company Lek's issue A was the most actively traded, rising 0.27 percent to 18,500 tolars on volume of 11,541 shares for total turnover of 211.5 million tolars.
Financial consultancy Finmedia was the leading decliner, shedding 4.48 percent to 15,990 on volume of 400 shares for total turnover of 6.4 million tolars.
Brokerage Nika was the top gainer, closing 3.81 percent higher at 3,950 on volume of 353 shares for total turnover of 1.4 million tolars.
